notes.text: Never two a's in a row — G¬(a ∧ Xa). Weakness is a constraint on the SHAPE of the machine, not a new way to judge a run: every strongly connected component must lie wholly inside F or wholly outside it. Here {ok, just saw a} is one SCC entirely inside F, and {dead} is one entirely outside. Acceptance is then decided exactly as Büchi would decide it.

That constraint is what makes a weak automaton easy to reason about: once a run settles into an SCC, its verdict is already fixed, because the whole component agrees. Break the shape — add an edge from "dead" back to "ok" so one SCC straddles F — and the app will say so before it runs, then fall back to plain Büchi acceptance.

meta.title: Never two a's in a row
meta.blurb: A deterministic weak automaton for a safety property. Weak decides like Büchi; its content is the promise that no SCC straddles F.
